# More Games (Plan 4) Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Add five freely licensed games and two test programs (`tape.tap`, `tune.sna`) to the built-in pack, each through the licence and playtest gates.

**Architecture:** Test programs are generated by `fmzx-pack testprogs` (`host/crates/fmzx-pack/src/testprogs.rs`) and committed in `games/test/`. Games are unmodified author files in `third_party/games/<id>/` with their licence evidence, listed in `games/games.toml` with a key map and a `demo` script. Host-core tests (`zx-tests`, `fmzx-pack` tests) and firmware tests in fm1-emu (`emu-gate`) cover each addition; the browser page's key maps follow the manifest.

**Tech Stack:** Rust host workspace (`host/`), C core (`core/zx`) through `zx-sys`, emu-gate on fm1-emu, REUSE, node for the web check.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-13-more-games-design.md` (approved). Background: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-11-zx48k-fm1-design.md` §5.3 (loading), §5.6 (game pack).

## Global Constraints

- Commit messages: a single line, no trailers (no Co-Authored-By). Never name any project other than this one and the games' own upstreams in files or commits.
- Device rule: never flash an FM-1, send it SysEx or open MIDI ports. Everything here runs on the host and in fm1-emu.
- Every game file is the author's file byte for byte, pinned by SHA-256 in its `README.md`. Never convert a file. A `.tzx` is not allowed (the core does not read it). The author's own `.sna`/`.z80` of the same release may replace the `.tap`.
- Licence gate: evidence is the author's own licence file or README in their repository or release. Copy it into `third_party/games/<id>/`, quote the sentence in the game's `README.md` with source URL, download URL and SHA-256. Every third-party part (loading screen, music, graphics, font, bundled library) must be the author's own or carry a licence permitting redistribution. One unclear part drops the game.
- A game that fails a gate is dropped at once: record it in `LICENSING.md` under "Considered and left out" with the reason, commit that, and report DONE_WITH_CONCERNS. Nobody writes to authors. If Traxtor fails, try Micro INC in its place.
- Picker order: `scroll`, `border`, `castaway`, then `sopwith`, `colony8`, `dino`, `oneway`, `traxtor` (or `microinc`), then `tape`, `tune` last.
- Every control a game needs to play is mapped (move, fire, jump, start, pause, and game actions). Key redefinition and sound toggles may stay unmapped. HOME and PLAY cannot be mapped (docs/controls.md).
- Names are at most 28 printable ASCII characters (`NAME_MAX`).
- No changes to `core/` to make a game work (that fails the game). No firmware C changes are expected; if one is needed for ten picker entries, it is in scope and needs `tools/fm1-docker` builds.
- Golden files change only by `FMZX_GOLDEN_UPDATE=1` runs whose diff you have inspected: hash files gain lines for new games and keep the old ones; any changed PNG is viewed before committing.
- Commands:
  - host: `cd host && cargo test --workspace --exclude emu-gate`
  - firmware tests (uses the existing device build in `build/fm1`; the pack is built from the manifest by the tests): `cd host && FMZX_FM1_BUILD=$PWD/../build/fm1 cargo test --release -p emu-gate`
  - licences: `reuse lint`
  - browser page: `tools/web-demo --check --skip-firmware`

## Review Focus

1. **A tape the core rejects as a whole.** `zx_tape_insert` validates every block; a release with an odd block (One-Way's `Wow.tap` has an empty data block) fails to start from the picker. Expected: the loader check in each game task catches it before commit (Task 3 step 2 procedure), and the release's other file is tried.
2. **Reset on a multi-load tape.** After HOME → reset game, `tape.tap` must load from its first block again and reach the loaded state again; the tape must not resume at its end. Test in Task 1.
3. **Games that ask "keyboard or joystick" at the title.** The key map must match the option the demo and the docs choose, or the controls do nothing. Each game task's demo picks the option its key map assumes, and `fw_report` proves the demo reaches play.
4. **Tests that find games by position.** Inserting games between Castaway and the test programs shifts indices. Tests for `tape` and `tune` look their index up by id from the manifest (Tasks 1-2), and the keymaps test counts against the manifest (Task 1).
5. **Picker with ten entries and long names.** "The Legend of Traxtor" and "Escape from Colony 8" must show in full and the list must scroll to the last entry. Task 8 checks the picker golden and starts the last game by turning SELECT.

### Task 1: `tape.tap`, the multi-load test program

**Files:**
- Modify: `host/crates/fmzx-pack/src/testprogs.rs` (new generator, `PROGRAMS` gains `("tape.tap", tape_tap)`, module docs gain a `tape.tap` section with the code listing as for the other two)
- Modify: `host/crates/zx-sys/src/lib.rs` (add `Machine::tape_pos(&self) -> u32`, reading `tape_pos`)
- Create: `games/test/tape.tap` (generated)
- Modify: `games/games.toml` (entry `id = "tape"`, `name = "Tape multi-load test"`, `file = "test/tape.tap"`, after Castaway)
- Modify: `host/crates/fmzx-pack/tests/testprogs.rs`, `host/crates/fmzx-pack/tests/keymaps.rs`, `host/crates/zx-tests/tests/golden/hashes.txt`, `host/crates/emu-gate/tests/fw_game.rs`, emu-gate goldens
- Modify: `docs/controls.md` or the manifest comment only if the program needs keys (it does not)

**Interfaces:**
- Produces: `pub fn tape_tap() -> Vec<u8>`; constants `pub const TAPE_WAIT_FRAMES: u32` (frames the code waits before loading) and `pub const TAPE_DONE_BORDER: u8 = 4`, `pub const TAPE_FAIL_BORDER: u8 = 2`; `Machine::tape_pos()`.

Program behaviour (exact code is yours; document it as a listing like the others):
1. Block pair 1: BASIC header + program, autostart line 10: `LOAD ""CODE: RANDOMIZE USR 32768` (same tokens as `zx-tests/tests/tape.rs` `autostart_loads_basic_and_code`).
2. Block pair 2: CODE header + code at 8000h.
3. Block 3: a headerless data block, flag FFh, 6,912 bytes: a screen image (bitmap + attributes) with a pattern that differs on every line (for example the line number in each byte) and non-default attributes.
4. The code sets border 1, waits `TAPE_WAIT_FRAMES` frames (EI; HALT under the ROM's IM 1), then calls LD-BYTES (0556h) with IX=4000h, DE=6912, A=FFh, carry set, then sets the border to `TAPE_DONE_BORDER` if carry is set on return, `TAPE_FAIL_BORDER` if not, and loops forever with interrupts on.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write failing tests** in `fmzx-pack/tests/testprogs.rs`:
  - `testprogs_reproducible`: `written.len() == 3` (from the `PROGRAMS` length, not a literal, so Task 2 needs no edit).
  - `tape_loads_its_data_block_after_starting`: insert `tape_tap()`, autostart; run frames; assert the border is 1 and the screen is not the data image for at least `TAPE_WAIT_FRAMES - 5` frames after the code starts; within 600 frames assert border line 100 == `TAPE_DONE_BORDER`, the 6,144 bitmap bytes and 768 attribute bytes equal the data block's payload, and `tape_pos() == tape.len()`.
  - In `fmzx-pack/tests/keymaps.rs`: replace `assert_eq!(json.matches("\"id\":").count(), 3)` with a count equal to `parse_manifest(...).game.len()`.
- [ ] **Step 2: Run** `cd host && cargo test -p fmzx-pack --test testprogs --test keymaps` — FAIL (no `tape_tap`).
- [ ] **Step 3: Implement** `tape_tap`, `tape_pos`, and add the manifest entry; run `cargo run -p fmzx-pack -- testprogs ../games/test` to write the file.
- [ ] **Step 4: Run** the host command (Global Constraints). The `each_game_runs` golden gains `game_tape_frame1500`: run once with `FMZX_GOLDEN_UPDATE=1`, check the diff adds exactly that line, re-run without it — PASS.
- [ ] **Step 5: Firmware tests** in `emu-gate/tests/fw_game.rs` (find the index of `tape` from `parse_manifest(games/games.toml)`, never a literal):
  - `tape_multiload_in_firmware`: start `tape` from the picker; at 1 s after start the LCD's border rows show colour 1; within 6 s they show colour 4 and the LCD matches golden `tape_loaded.png` (create with `FMZX_GOLDEN_UPDATE=1`, view it: the data pattern in the paper area, green border).
  - `tape_reloads_after_reset`: after the loaded state, HOME → reset game (as `fw_controls` does it); the border returns to 1 and later reaches 4 again with the same picture.
  Update the module doc comments that list the pack (`0 scroll, 1 border, 2 Castaway`) to say the test programs `tape`/`tune` are found by id. Run the firmware command — PASS (the picker golden may change: view it, update it).

### Task 2: `tune.sna`, the beeper music test program

**Files:**
- Modify: `host/crates/fmzx-pack/src/testprogs.rs` (generator, `PROGRAMS` gains `("tune.sna", tune_sna)`, doc section with listing)
- Create: `games/test/tune.sna`
- Modify: `games/games.toml` (entry `id = "tune"`, `name = "Beeper tune test"`, `file = "test/tune.sna"`, after `tape`)
- Modify: `host/crates/fmzx-pack/tests/testprogs.rs`, `host/crates/zx-tests/tests/golden/hashes.txt`, `host/crates/emu-gate/tests/fw_audio.rs`

**Interfaces:**
- Produces: `pub fn tune_sna() -> Vec<u8>`; `pub const TUNE_NOTES_HZ: [f64; 8] = [523.25, 587.33, 659.26, 698.46, 783.99, 880.00, 987.77, 1046.50]` (C5-C6, nominal); `pub const TUNE_NOTE_FRAMES: u32 = 25`; `pub const TUNE_HZ: [f64; 8]` (measured from the host beeper renderer, as `BORDER_TONE_HZ` was); `pub const TUNE_START_FRAME: u32` (first frame of the first note, if not 1).

Program behaviour: plays the eight notes in order, each `TUNE_NOTE_FRAMES` frames, and repeats forever, as a square wave on EAR (bit 4 of port FEh) with MIC 0; the screen shows something static (the note names or bars, your choice). Timing method is yours (interrupts on or off); document the half-period T-state counts per note and why the program's timing does not drift.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write failing tests** in `fmzx-pack/tests/testprogs.rs`:
  - `tune_pitches`: render 2 full passes of the tune with `Beeper` at `RATE`, skip 10 frames of settling, measure each note's frequency from zero crossings over its window minus 2 frames at each end; each within 1% of `TUNE_NOTES_HZ[i]` and within 0.2% of `TUNE_HZ[i]`.
  - `tune_has_no_gaps`: over frames 10-410, consecutive beeper edges (T-states made absolute across frames by adding 69,888 per frame) are never further apart than 1.02 × the longest half-period, and every frame has at least one edge.
- [ ] **Step 2: Run** `cd host && cargo test -p fmzx-pack --test testprogs` — FAIL.
- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**, write `games/test/tune.sna` with `fmzx-pack testprogs`, add the manifest entry, measure and record `TUNE_HZ`.
- [ ] **Step 4: Run** the host command; golden gains `game_tune_frame300` only (inspect diff) — PASS.
- [ ] **Step 5: Firmware test** `tune_pitches_in_firmware` in `emu-gate/tests/fw_audio.rs`: find `tune`'s index by id from the manifest, start it, capture the firmware's audio as `tone_frequency` does, measure each note's window with the same zero-crossing method; each within 2% of `TUNE_HZ[i]`, and no window of 20 ms is silent. Run the firmware command — PASS.
- [ ] **Step 6: Commit:** `git commit -m "Add the tune.sna beeper music test program: eight notes, pitch and gap tests in the core and the firmware"`

### Game task procedure (Tasks 3-7)

Each game task follows these steps; the task itself gives the specifics.

- [ ] **Step 1: Fetch** the release file into a new empty directory under `build/games-fetch/<id>/` (git-ignored `build/`), record its SHA-256 and size. Read every licence file, README and credits in the release and the source repository.
- [ ] **Step 2: Loader check.** Walk the `.tap`'s blocks (flag, length, checksum valid; header types and load addresses) and write the block list into the game's `README.md`. It must be a standard ROM-loader tape (BASIC loader, standard blocks; a loader that calls LD-BYTES 0556h is fine) that `Machine::tape_insert` accepts. Run it in the host core for 1,500 frames after `tape_autostart` (or 300 after `load_sna`) and confirm the title screen appears. Failure → try the author's own `.sna`/`.z80` of the same release if one exists; otherwise the game fails the gate.
- [ ] **Step 3: Licence gate.** Check the points the task lists. Pass → copy the evidence files into `third_party/games/<id>/` (unmodified, names as in the release, e.g. `README.release.txt`), add the game file, write `third_party/games/<id>/README.md` in Castaway's shape (SPDX header; table: file, SHA-256, release URL, source URL and commit, licence + SPDX; quoted licence statements; attribution; block list; controls and the FM-1 map). Add `REUSE.toml` annotations for the game file and evidence files (as Castaway's), the attribution to `LICENSING.md` "The built-in games", and any new licence text to `LICENSES/` (REUSE expects `LICENSES/<SPDX>.txt`).
- [ ] **Step 4: Manifest.** Add the `[[game]]` entry at its picker position (Global Constraints), with a comment block like Castaway's (controls, how the demo plays), `[game.keys]` overriding the default map where the game uses keys, `crop` if the game's score sits at an edge, and a `demo` that gets past the title into play within the report window and keeps the game moving for about 20 s (syntax: docs/controls.md and the Castaway entry).
- [ ] **Step 5: Tests.** Run the host command with `FMZX_GOLDEN_UPDATE=1` once; the diff must only add `game_<id>_frame<N>`; re-run without — PASS. Run `cd host && FMZX_FM1_BUILD=$PWD/../build/fm1 cargo test --release -p emu-gate --test fw_report -- --nocapture` — the new game's line appears and the "demo got into play" check passes. Run the whole firmware command — PASS (update and view the picker PNG if it changed). `reuse lint` — compliant.
- [ ] **Step 6: Docs.** `docs/controls.md` gains the game's FM-1 map if it documents per-game maps (follow what it does for Castaway); `README.md`'s game list names the game.
- [ ] **Step 7: Commit:** `git commit -m "Add <Name> to the built-in pack: <licence>, unmodified <file>, key map and demo"`

### Task 3: ZX Sopwith (`sopwith`)

- Release: https://github.com/neilrackett/zxspectrum-sopwith — use `sopwith.sna` (49,179 bytes) from https://github.com/neilrackett/zxspectrum-sopwith/releases/download/latest/sopwith.sna. The tag is rolling: record the release's commit (from the GitHub API or the release page) alongside the SHA-256.
- Licence: GPL-3.0-or-later (repo `LICENSE`, README sentence "Released under the GNU General Public License v3.0 …", SPDX headers in the source). Gate points: the README's statement that the original Sopwith (David L. Clark) is GPL-2.0-or-later, confirmed against an original-source repository (e.g. https://github.com/fragglet/sdl-sopwith README/COPYING); no excluded art. SPDX for the file: `GPL-3.0-or-later`.
- Controls: Q/A pitch, O/P throttle, SPACE fire, F flip, B bomb, H home, M sound, 1 abandon; Kempston flies and fires. Map: Kempston on F3-A3 and C5-G5 (the defaults), F/B/H on nearby notes or buttons, documented.
- Picker name: `ZX Sopwith`.

### Task 4: Escape from Colony 8 (`colony8`)

- Release: https://usebox.net/jjm/colony8/colony8.zip → `colony8.tap` (33,045 bytes). Pin the zip's and the tap's SHA-256.
- Licence: MIT in the zip's `README.txt` ("Escape from Colony 8, version 1.0 / Copyright (C) 2014 by Juan J. Martinez"). Gate points: the usebox.net footer (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 "unless stated otherwise") is recorded and the release's MIT applies, as for Castaway; no third-party credits; SPDX `MIT`.
- Controls: O/P/Q/A, SPACE fire (hold to charge), H pause; Kempston and Sinclair. Demo chooses the option the map assumes.
- Picker name: `Escape from Colony 8`.

### Task 5: ZX Dino (`dino`)

- File: `dino.tap` from https://github.com/foxweb/zxdino at a pinned commit (raw URL with the commit hash, not `master`). 9,504 bytes per the research.
- Licence: MIT (`LICENSE`, "Copyright © 2026 Kukovnikov Bonifas"). Gate points: the sprites are the author's own (repo `sprites/`, `art.py`, commit history), not copied from Chrome's game; SPDX `MIT`.
- Controls: SPACE or Q jump, A or CAPS SHIFT duck, any key starts. Map jump to F#3/G#3 and C5-G5, duck to G3.
- Picker name: `ZX Dino`.

### Task 6: A World of One-Way (`oneway`)

- Repo: https://github.com/Serdjuk/A-World-of-One-way — candidates `Wow.tap` (tree, pinned commit) or the 0.41 release zip https://github.com/Serdjuk/A-World-of-One-way/releases/download/0.41/A-World-of-One-way_0.41.zip. `Wow.tap` has an empty data block (Review Focus 1): if `tape_insert` rejects it, use the release zip's file if that one passes, else the game fails the gate.
- Licence: Apache-2.0 (repo `LICENSE`) and the MIT beeper engine by Juan J. Martínez (header in its source; keep the notice in the README). Gate points: the font (`font.SpecCHR`) and title screen must be shown to be the author's own (source comments, commit history, credits); any unclear origin fails the gate. Add `LICENSES/Apache-2.0.txt` and correct `LICENSING.md`'s "Nothing in the repository itself is under the Apache License." SPDX for the file: `Apache-2.0 AND MIT`.
- Controls: Q/A/O/P, Sinclair 1/2; CAPS SHIFT + ENTER menu; shop keys 1/2. Map directions on F3-A3, the shop keys and the menu chord on buttons.
- Picker name: `A World of One-Way`.
